title: Numeric and Mathematical Operations
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of numeric and mathematical operations in a Classic ASP application.
Identify and describe at least two syllabus subtopics: Integer-like and decimal values and Numeric conversion functions.
Inspect a minimal example and define a reproducible normal-case and failure-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study numeric and mathematical operations as part of Classic ASP development and legacy maintenance. The lesson follows the attached ASP curriculum topic 24 and uses the syllabus subtopics as the coverage checklist.
content.why_it_matters: Numeric and Mathematical Operations matters because Classic ASP behavior crosses a server-side scripting engine, IIS configuration, request/response boundaries, and often COM or ADO dependencies. A small, explicit test helps distinguish intended behavior from runtime-specific behavior.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: VBScript is the scripting language used by many Classic ASP applications. In 'Numeric and Mathematical Operations', make input types, empty/null values, scope, and evaluation order explicit: Variant values can change behavior based on the value they contain, and a value read from Request is still untrusted text until validated. Use Option Explicit and small, testable procedures to make mistakes easier to detect.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
content_blocks.text: The lesson explicitly covers: Integer-like and decimal values; Numeric conversion functions; Rounding and absolute values; Division and remainder operations; Formatting numeric output; Handling invalid numeric input. Treat these subtopics as connected requirements. For each one, be able to define the concept, identify where it appears in a Classic ASP application, and name one test or diagnostic that would verify it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Numeric and Mathematical Operations
content_blocks.code:
<%
Dim rawTotal, amount
rawTotal = "19.50"
If IsNumeric(rawTotal) Then
  amount = CCur(rawTotal)
  Response.Write CStr(amount)
Else
  Response.Write "Invalid amount"
End If
%>
content_blocks.run_instructions: Currency/date parsing is locale-sensitive. Parse against an explicit input contract and test the server locale before relying on formatted output. content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Use a local Classic ASP page. Change one value or statement at a time, capture the observed output, and check at least one empty, malformed, or boundary value. The source syllabus treats Classic ASP as a legacy maintenance technology, not as ASP.NET or a default choice for new web projects.

content_blocks.title: Guided workflow
content_blocks.text: 1. Start with a minimal local example of numeric and mathematical operations. 2. Trace its inputs, state changes, dependencies, and output. 3. Test a normal case, a missing/malformed case, and one permission/provider/runtime failure. 4. Write down the exact expected and observed result before changing another variable.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small, reviewable demonstration of numeric and mathematical operations using synthetic data. Include at least one of these syllabus concepts: Integer-like and decimal values. State the expected result first, then add one invalid or boundary case and explain how your program should behave.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating legacy runtime behavior as universal.
common_mistakes.why: IIS versions, Windows lifecycle, COM registration/bitness, and ADO providers can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the actual server/provider versions and validate on a disposable test site.

common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing records, expired sessions, permissions, timeouts, and malformed data reveal different failure modes.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, negative, and boundary cases with expected outcomes.

common_mistakes.why: Detailed errors can reveal paths, SQL text, configuration, and component information.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep diagnostics in restricted server-side logs and return a generic message with a reference ID.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming syntax alone proves the application works.
common_mistakes.why: IIS configuration, permissions, COM activation, database providers, and response behavior are external dependencies.
common_mistakes.fix: Run against the documented local test host and record exact evidence.

common_mistakes.why: Query strings, form fields, cookies, and hidden controls remain client-controlled.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate on the server and apply authorization and output encoding at the appropriate boundary.
